name: IEC logic negation at input
summary: Small circle where an input meets an outline: an external 0 produces the internal 1 (active) state.
description: The negation circle at an input means that the external 0 state produces the internal 1 state of the element. It is a pure logic statement: to relate it to voltage levels, the drawing must declare positive or negative logic. TI's public overview notes that this is the older form, with the polarity triangle now preferred in device data books.

On functional logic diagrams for control systems, input negation is a compact way to show normally-closed or fault-healthy signals entering a gate without drawing a separate inverter. The reader should confirm the declared logic convention before relating a circle to a contact state or voltage.
A negation circle does not specify how the inversion is implemented. It may be a separate inverter, an internal feature of the device, or a negated contact in a PLC rung.
readingNotes: Check the sheet note for positive or negative logic.
Do not confuse the circle with a connection dot or terminal.
drawingChecklist: Draw the circle touching the outline.
Declare the logic convention on the drawing.
Avoid mixing negation circles and polarity triangles on one sheet.
distinction: The polarity indicator triangle states an active-low level directly and does not depend on a declared logic convention.
